sourcedFrom: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Hawkeye Long-Range Target is a DETACHABLE-MAGAZINE bolt rifle and it has its own Ruger book — not the floorplate Hawkeye manual. ⚠ That difference runs right through the strip: routine cleaning needs the bolt AND the magazine out, and taking the stock off means three screws and a CROSS BOLT through the stock behind the magazine well. ⛔ The firing pin assembly is permanent here too, and it is under great spring pressure.

steps.title: ⚠ THIS MANUAL COVERS the LRT, the LRH and the Scout — every other Hawkeye is in a DIFFERENT MANUAL
steps.action: Ruger scopes this manual on its own cover: the LRT and the LRH share the Scout rifle's general operational characteristics, each carries its extra features in a manual INSERT at the back, and ⛔ for all other Hawkeye rifles you are sent to the Hawkeye & Guide Gun manual, PM182. If your rifle is a Hunter, an African or a Guide Gun, it is covered by a separate manual and not by this one. ⚠ And the insert itself points back the other way — "Please refer to the enclosed Scout Rifle manual for additional information and important warnings" — which is what this PDF actually is: the Scout manual with the LRT and LRH inserts bound at the back. The strip and the cleaning below come from that main body, and they apply to your rifle because Ruger says on the cover that they do.
steps.prose: The maker drawing its own line between two of its manuals is worth more than any inference we could make about which one covers what.
steps.aside: Please refer to the enclosed Scout Rifle manual for additional information and important warnings.
steps.quote: The RUGER® Hawkeye® Long-Range Target (“LRT”) and the RUGER® Hawkeye® Long-Range Hunter (“LRH”) rifles have the same general operational characteristics as the RUGER® Scout rifle. However, each rifle has additional features as described in the manual inserts located at the back of this manual. For all other Hawkeye® rifles refer to the Hawkeye® & Guide Gun instruction manual (PM182).
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Cover, p.1

steps.title: Safety to LOAD-UNLOAD, bolt fully back, chamber checked
steps.action: Point the rifle safely and put the safety in the "Load-Unload" position. Lift the bolt handle FULLY and pull it completely to the rear to eject any chambered cartridge, then check the chamber is empty by eye.
steps.prose: Lift fully, then pull. A partially lifted handle drags the extractor and can leave a round sitting in the receiver.
steps.quote: 2. Lift the bolt handle fully and then pull it completely to the rear to eject
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly, step 2, p.22

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine out — and a chambered round can STILL fire
steps.action: Remove the magazine. ⛔ Ruger prints the reason in the same step: even with the magazine removed, a cartridge remaining in the chamber can still be fired. Magazine out is not the same as unloaded.
steps.prose: This is the sentence that exists because people believe the opposite.
steps.quote: 4. Remove the magazine. REMEMBER that even though the magazine has been removed, a cartridge remaining in the chamber can still be fired!
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly, step 4, p.22

steps.title: Bolt out — pull back and PIVOT THE BOLT STOP open together
steps.action: Open the bolt and pull it to the rear while at the same time pivoting the bolt stop open — left side of the receiver on a right-handed rifle. Both motions together; the bolt will not clear a closed stop.
steps.prose: Same action as every Hawkeye. It is the whole field strip.
steps.quote: 5. To remove the bolt: Open bolt and pull to the rear while at the same time pivoting open the bolt stop
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly, step 5, p.22

steps.title: ⛔ Firing pin OUT of the bolt is fine — APART is not
steps.action: With the bolt out and the firing pin cocked, a pin or nail through the "disassembly hole" in the cocking piece levers the firing pin assembly out. ⛔ Do not disassemble the assembly itself: Ruger states it is intended to be permanent, the parts are under great spring pressure, and they could fly apart with force enough to cause serious injury.
steps.prose: The pin or nail should be close to the hole's diameter and at least two inches long, so it can actually lever rather than just poke.
steps.quote: 6. To remove firing pin assembly from bolt: With bolt out of the rifle and firing pin cocked, insert a pin or nail into the “disassembly hole” in the cocking piece.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly, step 6, p.23
steps.warn: CAUTION: The firing pin assembly is intended to be a permanent assembly and should not be disassembled. The parts are under great spring pressure and if disassembled could fly apart with sufficient force to cause serious injury.

steps.title: ⚠ Stock off — TWO screws AND a cross bolt through the magazine well
steps.action: This is where the LRT parts company with a floorplate Hawkeye. Loosen and remove the screw holding the Front Mounting Lug; then the screw holding the Trigger Guard / Magazine well; then the CROSS BOLT that runs through the stock at the REAR of the magazine well. Only then does the trigger guard/magazine well come out.
steps.prose: Three fasteners, and the cross bolt is the one people do not look for because no floorplate rifle has it.
steps.quote: c. Loosen and remove the Cross Bolt that runs through the stock at the rear of the magazine well.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly, step 7c, p.23

steps.title: ⚠ Routine cleaning needs only the BOLT and the MAGAZINE out
steps.action: Ruger's own scope for routine work on this rifle: remove the bolt and the magazine, and that is all the disassembly required. ⛔ Confirm the rifle and its magazine are unloaded before any of it.
steps.prose: Note the difference from the floorplate book — magazine, not floorplate. Same sentence, different rifle.
steps.quote: 1. For routine cleaning it is necessary only to remove the bolt and magazine.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Care and Cleaning, step 1, p.27
steps.warn: WARNING: BEFORE CLEANING, BE CERTAIN THE RIFLE AND ITS MAGAZINE ARE UNLOADED.

steps.title: Bore: solvent patch push-pull, then the brush FULL LENGTH
steps.action: Push-pull a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times. Then run a solvent-wetted brush the full length of the bore as many times as it takes to remove the fouling completely.
steps.prose: On a target rifle the bore is the whole point. Full-length passes, and as many as it takes rather than a fixed count.
steps.quote: 2. Push-pull a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Care and Cleaning, step 2, p.27

steps.title: Receiver, then a VERY LIGHT coat of oil
steps.action: Clean solvent-wetted patch over every reachable surface inside the receiver, toothbrush for caked dirt. Then wipe all surfaces — internal and external — with a VERY LIGHT coat of oil, because oil collects dirt particles that interfere with reliable functioning.
steps.prose: Light is the operative word on a rifle whose accuracy depends on the bedding staying clean.
steps.aside: Reassemble the rifle and carefully wipe all solvent, lubricating and preservative preparations from the stock.
steps.quote: Wipe all surfaces – internal and external – with a very light coat of oil.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Care and Cleaning, step 4, p.27

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the bore before a live round
steps.action: Before the rifle is loaded, confirm the bore is clear. Ruger's warning is explicit: firing with oil, grease or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may damage the rifle and seriously injure the shooter and those nearby.
steps.prose: A patch left in a match barrel is a bulged barrel, and it happens to careful people at the end of a careful clean.
steps.quote: Firing a rifle with oil, grease, or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the rifle and serious injury to the shooter and those nearby.
steps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Warning — Lubrication, p.28

deepSteps.title: ⛔ A lost spring or plunger is NOT substituted
deepSteps.action: Ruger's standing rule before the action comes apart: if a spring or plunger becomes lost, do not use a substitute — spring tension is a safety property. Work over a covered bench so an escaped plunger is still findable.
deepSteps.prose: Shallow nap rug or an old coarse blanket is Ruger's own suggestion, and it is a good one.
deepSteps.quote: If a spring or plunger become lost do not use a substitute. Springs of correct tension are vital to the safe and reliable performance of firearms.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Disassembly — Warning, p.22

deepSteps.title: ⚠ LRT INSERT — length of pull is a stack of three 1/2 inch spacers
deepSteps.action: The rifle ships with THREE 1/2 inch spacers — one fitted, two in the box — giving 12-3/4 to 14-1/4 inches of pull in half-inch steps. Safety on SAFE, chamber AND magazine checked empty, magazine out, bolt fully closed and locked. Then the allen wrench supplied with the rifle takes the recoil pad screws out; stack or remove spacers and refit. ⛔ Do not overtighten those screws.
deepSteps.prose: Set the length of pull BEFORE the cheek piece — Ruger says so, and it is the right order because the cheek piece position depends on where your face lands.
deepSteps.quote: Each RUGER® Hawkeye® Long-Range Target rifle comes from the factory with three 1/2” spacers (one installed on the rifle and two packaged separately) that allow you to adjust the length of pull from 12-3/4” to 14-1/4” in onehalf-inch increments.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Manual Insert PM656 — Length of Pull Adjustment

deepSteps.title: ⚠ LRT INSERT — the cheek piece moves four ways on one cam lever
deepSteps.action: The cheek piece adjusts forward and rearward AND up and down. Raise the cam lever to free it, move it where you want it, and lower the lever. ⚠ Ruger's own note: it may be useful to set the length of pull before adjusting the cheek piece.
deepSteps.prose: One lever, two axes. Loosen it once and set both rather than chasing them separately.
deepSteps.quote: 1. The cheek piece can be adjusted forward and rearward and up and down. Raise the cam lever on the cheek piece to change its position (see Figure 2).
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Manual Insert PM656 — Adjusting the Cheek Piece

deepSteps.title: Stainless is MORE resistant, not immune
deepSteps.action: If your rifle is stainless, Ruger's note is worth reading rather than assuming: stainless components are relatively MORE resistant to corrosion than blued steel — not exempt from it. External surfaces exposed to handling or the elements get cleaned and wiped dry after use.
deepSteps.prose: A target rifle that lives in a case between matches is exactly the one that rusts under a fingerprint.
deepSteps.quote: External surfaces most subject to rusting from handling, or from exposure to the elements should be cleaned and wiped dry after use
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Care and Cleaning, p.28

deepSteps.title: Long-term storage — clean, strip to the manual's depth, keep the small parts
deepSteps.action: For extended storage, clean the rifle thoroughly and disassemble it to the extent this manual describes, putting pins and similar easily mislaid parts somewhere they will be found.
deepSteps.prose: "To the extent described elsewhere in this manual" is the book bounding its own depth, and it is the honest end of this guide too.
deepSteps.quote: 6. If the rifle is to be stored for an extended period, clean the rifle thoroughly.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® SCOUT, HAWKEYE® LRT, & HAWKEYE® LRH BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM280) — PM280 — Care and Cleaning, step 6, p.27

cleaning.name: ROUTINE — BOLT AND MAGAZINE OUT
tasks: Rifle and magazine confirmed unloaded first
Bolt and magazine removed — that is all the strip routine cleaning needs
Solvent-wetted patch push-pulled through the bore several times
Solvent-wetted brush the FULL length, as many passes as it takes
Clean solvent patch over every reachable receiver surface; toothbrush on caked dirt

cleaning.name: OIL AND STOCK
tasks: VERY LIGHT coat of oil inside and out — oil collects dirt
All solvent, lubricant and preservative wiped off the stock on reassembly
Stainless external surfaces cleaned and wiped DRY after handling or exposure

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ Firing pin assembly out of the bolt, never apart

reassembly: Firing pin assembly back into the bolt, intact.
Trigger guard / magazine well into the stock.
Cross bolt through the stock behind the magazine well.
Trigger-guard screw, then the Front Mounting Lug screw.
Bolt in with the bolt stop pivoted clear; magazine seated and latched.
⛔ Bore confirmed clear and dry before a live round.
fncheck: Chamber checked empty by eye, magazine out. Cycle the bolt through full travel — it should lift, run and lock without dragging, and the bolt stop should retain it at the rear. Seat an EMPTY magazine and confirm the latch holds it, then press the latch forward and confirm it drops free. Work the three-position safety and confirm the middle "Load-Unload" position opens the bolt with the trigger blocked. ⛔ Confirm the bore is clear of patches, bristles, oil and grease before any live round.
